changedBeliefs: Collapsing a homogeneous MultiExecuteRequest's per-member execute loop into one private C call is not enough while every member remains an independent SQLite autocommit. The public 5,120-insert gate improved 17.7% in candidate-first order but only 3.6% in baseline-first order, missing the predeclared 10% reproduced bar.

The envelope adds a real fixed cost rather than merely failing to beat noise: an integer-only no-op UPDATE burst regressed 17.7% / 13.9% across the order flip. Whole-group allocateBatchParams packing, result-buffer materialization, and suffix repacking after errors can cost more than the scalar path's already-specialized one-row encoder and repeated FFI calls.

Preserving independent outcomes inside a native loop has hidden correctness and resource constraints. A retry must handle sqlite3_reset commit errors, deliver the dirty-dependency union before affected futures resolve, retain failed-statement side effects, clear SQLITE_STATIC bindings before freeing the arena, make the result ABI explicit, cap aggregate variable-width payloads, and guard main-isolate diagnostic latency while the writer mutex is held.
nextSignals: Keep exp 180's scalar per-member worker loop. Do not retry a whole-group native parameter/result arena under the current MultiExecuteRequest representation.

Reopen only if transport already supplies a bounded native-ready arena or another design removes group repacking; require at least 10% on public 100/200-member insert bursts in both process orders, neutral 2/8/32-member bursts, and BLOB peak-RSS plus diagnostics-latency guards.
Treat true group commit as the separate exp 197 semantic/API frontier. Exp 257 shows that collapsing only Dart/native orchestration while retaining N autocommits does not capture that ceiling.

claims.text: A one-call native interpreter that preserves independent autocommits does not clear the writer-burst bar: homogeneous inserts improved 17.7% then only 3.6% across the order flip, while integer-only no-op updates regressed 17.7% and 13.9%.
